## Daoism quotes

Daoism (Taoism) names philosophical and religious currents oriented to the Dao—the Way—often emphasizing naturalness, transformation, and non-coercive action.

21 passages · 2 voices in this archive selection

### Overview

The Daodejing and Zhuangzi are foundational philosophical texts. Themes include wuwei (non-forcing action), critique of rigid naming, soft power, and perspectival freedom. Religious Daoism develops parallel practices; this page focuses on philosophical quotations in the archive.

### Historical notes

Classical Daoist texts take shape in the Warring States period; later commentary and religious movements expand the tradition across East Asia and into global translation.

### Core ideas

-   Align with the Dao rather than forcing outcomes.
-   Softness and flexibility can overcome rigidity.
-   Fixed distinctions and names can distort living reality.
-   Skillful spontaneity emerges from practiced attunement.

### FAQ

#### What is Daoism?

It is a family of Chinese traditions centered on the Dao, naturalness, and often wuwei—acting without forcing.

#### Who are the main Daoist philosophers?

Laozi and Zhuangzi are the most-read philosophical figures in English, though the textual history is complex.

#### Where can I find Daoist quotes?
